title: Prompt caching (Claude API Docs)
relevance_note: Vendor caching doc detailing cache isolation boundaries, invalidation hierarchy, and accounting fields (reads vs writes vs post-breakpoint tokens).
reason_included: Concrete prompt-caching mechanics and invalidation rules that directly constrain context compilation and compaction strategies.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Cache invalidation follows a hierarchy: `tools` → `system` → `messages`; changes at a higher level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels.

For concurrent requests, a cache entry becomes available only after the first response begins; to get cache hits for parallel requests, the doc instructs waiting for the first response before sending subsequent requests.

The doc defines cache accounting fields and a token breakdown where total input tokens are calculated as `cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens`, and `input_tokens` counts only tokens after the last breakpoint.

Starting February 5, 2026, Anthropic prompt caching switches from organization-level to workspace-level isolation for the Claude API (and Azure AI Foundry preview), isolating caches per workspace for data separation; Bedrock and Vertex maintain organization-level isolation.
